text:
Jia Wang: Ran a set of perfetto traces against staging10 under a production-like QPS and saw recurring 120ms tail spikes. attaching a link to the blob and the perfetto UI view. can someone help interpret the kernel timeline?

Ryan Patel: I skimmed the trace — there's a kernel switch right before the long tail where the runtime falls back to a different attention kernel. looks like a selection decision at ~76ms into the request.

Sara Kim: do we have kv-cache metrics in the trace? sometimes kv misses + replays amplify the switch.

perf-bot: perfetto capture uploaded to gs://redwood-traces/staging/1791234567_gpu.pb (:file_folder:)

Mike O'Connor: can you paste the perfetto slice query you used? i'll pull it up.

Jia Wang: here's the ad-hoc query i used in the perfetto SQL panel to find kernel slices:
```
select ts, dur, name, track_id from slice where name like '%kernel%' order by ts limit 50;
```
gives the kernel timeline. the interesting bit is a dense cluster of small kernels, then a long "attention_v2_fallback" slice.

Ryan Patel: i also ran an nsys capture locally. the nvtx ranges show the decision happens in kernel_selection.cpp:~line 412 where fallback triggers for sequences > 1024. hotspot in the launched kernel is `launch_attention` (~40% of GPU time).

Sara Kim: might be related to batching heuristics. if the gateway's batching window combines one long sequence with short ones we can force a fallback. check the gateway span boundaries — i suspect we're double counting queuing vs compute.

Jia Wang: timeline breakdown from perfetto flame view i exported: client->gateway RPC: 9-12ms, gateway batching/wait: 60-90ms (variable), runtime queue -> kernel launch: 8-10ms, kernel exec: 30-80ms (spikes). so the big contributor is gateway batching aligning weirdly with seq_len=2048 runs.

Mike O'Connor: reproducible locally with this command:
```
nsys profile -o trace_1791234567 --trace=nvtx,cuda python loadtest.py --target staging10 --qps 50 --seq_len 2048 --batch_window_ms 10
```
that produced almost identical kernel selection patterns.

Sara Kim: try enabling kv cache debug logging to confirm misses: add `--kv-debug` to runtime flags, and set `KV_CACHE_LOGGING=1` in env. if misses spike during those windows that's a smoking gun.

Ryan Patel: small note — i saw a perf regression introduced around commit ab12cd3 where the kernel selector's threshold changed from 1536->1024 for the quant kernel. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/842

Jia Wang: good catch. that would explain why long sequences now choose fallback more often. we need to test reverting threshold or improving kernel availability.

Mike O'Connor: i'll run a focused perfetto + nsys capture on staging10 with seq_len=2048 and kv debug on. will post the pb and nvprof timeline later today.

Sara Kim: can someone also check gateway code for batching heuristics? if we can avoid mixing very long seqs with batches it's an operational mitigation. maybe add gating on seq_len to separate queues.

Ryan Patel: agreed. also we should mark this for a regression alert in the evals dashboards — add a check for the kernel selector distribution.

Jia Wang: plan: (1) Mike runs nsys + perfetto with `--kv-debug` on staging10 (assigned) (2) Ryan will diff kernel selection code and propose revert or improved threshold (3) Sara will prototype gating by seq_len in gateway batching. i'll collect traces and open a follow-up ticket with attached perfetto pb and nsys output.

Mike O'Connor: on it. running now. tagging @ryan and @sara for followups. :mag:

perf-bot: scheduled nsys capture job started on staging10 (job id: 2026-03-18-001)

Jia Wang: thanks all. if anyone spots anything obvious in the uploads ping in this thread. :thumbsup:
